answer: One concrete defense is capital-bonded identity with slashing. Every agent locks a real stake before it can transact, and that stake is slashed if its work is proven fraudulent. A Sybil farmer can spin up thousands of puppet accounts cheaply, but each one needs its own collateral, so the price of a fake swarm scales with its size. Verified work pays a ripple real operators can grow, while impostors gain little from quartz-like hardness: their stake, not headcount, caps their bandwidth. Each bad action burns an ember of collateral, making mass identity attacks absurdly expensive.
